subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 61-year-old woman with resistant hypertension enters a clinical trial of an investigational agent that lowers blood pressure by inhibiting a vascular smooth-muscle enzyme. In vitro, the agent binds a site on the enzyme that is distinct from the substrate-binding site, and raising the substrate concentration does not restore the maximal rate. Kinetic analysis shows an unchanged apparent Km with a decreased Vmax.
question: Which of the following Lineweaver-Burk patterns is most likely to be observed with this agent?

options.text: Lines intersecting on the y-axis with an unchanged x-intercept
Lines intersecting on the x-axis with a higher y-intercept
A single line identical to the uninhibited reaction
Lines intersecting to the left of the y-axis with both intercepts changed

explanation_correct: Binding to a site distinct from the active site without competition for substrate describes noncompetitive inhibition, which lowers Vmax but leaves Km unchanged. On the double-reciprocal plot the x-intercept (-1/Km) is unchanged, whereas the y-intercept (1/Vmax) increases, so the lines cross exactly on the x-axis. Because the inhibitor does not compete with substrate, adding more substrate cannot restore the maximal velocity.

explanation_incorrect.A: Intersection on the y-axis characterizes competitive inhibition, in which Vmax is preserved and apparent Km increases; here the agent is not substrate-competitive.
explanation_incorrect.B: Parallel lines indicate uncompetitive inhibition, in which both Km and Vmax decrease and the inhibitor binds only the enzyme-substrate complex.
explanation_incorrect.D: Identical lines would indicate no inhibition at all; the agent clearly decreases the maximal rate.
explanation_incorrect.E: Intersection left of the y-axis indicates mixed inhibition, in which both apparent Km and Vmax change; here Km is unchanged.

educationalObjective: Noncompetitive inhibition produces Lineweaver-Burk lines that intersect on the x-axis because Km is unchanged while Vmax (1/y-intercept) decreases.
